chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who advances a loan in wheat and dates for one hundred dirhams, and when the time comes for him to take what is due to him, his debtor comes to him and says: 'By Allah, I do not have with me except half of what is yours, so take from me if you wish, half of what is yours in wheat and the other half in silver coins.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm if he takes the silver from him as he gave it to him.'
ai.seo_question: Can a debtor repay a loan of grain with a combination of grain and silver coins?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the rules of *Qard* (loan) and *Bay' al-Madmun* (sale of guaranteed goods) by permitting a creditor to accept silver coins (*Wariq*) in lieu of the remaining wheat or dates owed. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the settlement of commodity loans, allowing for mixed payments when the debtor lacks the full quantity in kind, provided the agreed-upon value is maintained. It underscores the principle that the specific form of repayment can be adapted to the debtor's capacity without invalidating the debt obligation.
